claims.text: Traditional EAM references inadequately represent the wide variety of atomic configurations in ab initio multicomponent liquids.
Replacing EAM references with a DNN potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The DNN potential should be trained on diverse ab initio liquid configurations and refined through active learning.
A DNN potential can represent both solid and liquid states near melting.
Including a wide variety of ab initio liquid snapshots in training improves phase-space overlap between the reference simulation and the target system.
Training on liquid configurations enables the DNN to reproduce the target energy landscape more accurately.
Training on liquid configurations enables the DNN to reproduce liquid structural fluctuations more accurately.
Improved reproduction of the energy landscape and structural fluctuations reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The DNN reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Reduced path mismatch will improve free-energy predictions for both solid and liquid phases near melting.
The proposed method is applicable from approximately 3000 K to 3600 K.
The proposed method is applicable to alloys containing five or more principal elements, especially equimolar or near-equimolar systems.
The method's performance for simpler alloys or temperatures far below melting is not established.
The magnitude of path-mismatch reduction may vary with alloy composition and simulation details.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant reduction exceeding 30% relative to the EAM control would falsify the hypothesis.
Free-energy results outside expected uncertainty bounds would falsify the hypothesis.
